why: The Ω ambiguity gate compares Ĥ_route against 0.90, while the GML field carries absolute entropy measurements with a declared bound. Nothing declared the relationship between the two, so a consumer could silently compare or substitute them. They are different quantities with different normalisation denominators, so the relationship has to be stated and the only sanctioned bridge has to be an explicit, dimensionless opt-in axis.

router.definition: H / ln|Eligible| over the eligible W·C·R distribution
router.default_status: provisional, documented in docs/GLOSSARY.md as Ĥ_route > 0.90

field.units: absolute field units with a declared bound (entropy_bound)
field.normalisation: none: the field declares an absolute value and its bound, not a distribution

relationship.law: the two surfaces are different quantities and are not interconvertible; neither may be substituted for the other
relationship.why_not_convertible: Ĥ_route divides by ln|Eligible| (a property of the candidate set); the field divides by nothing and declares entropy_bound (a property of the field). A ratio of field values is not a distribution entropy, so deriving one from the other would be a fabricated normalisation.

sanctioned_bridge.kind: explicit, dimensionless, router-facing opt-in axis on a FieldParamRecord
sanctioned_bridge.detail: a field that wants to move the gate must speak the router's unit and say so by name; a field that only declares local_entropy/entropy_bound is refused rather than converted

unsanctioned: dividing local_entropy by entropy_bound and calling the result a distribution entropy
accepting a threshold from a request payload

precedence.law: the gate threshold is host configuration or a loaded, declared record axis; a request payload can never move it
precedence.payload_claims: ignored, and the fact that a claim was ignored is reported

provenance.recorded_on: every routing decision, as omega_threshold + omega_threshold_source + omega_threshold_detail

invariants.EB1: the router threshold is a dimensionless number in (0, 1]; the field entropy is absolute; the two are never compared without a declared conversion
invariants.EB2: no implicit conversion exists: a record that declares only local_entropy / entropy_bound / entropy_spike / entropy_delta is refused with no_router_threshold_axis
invariants.EB3: the only sanctioned source is an explicit omega_entropy_threshold axis whose value lies in (0, 1]
invariants.EB4: threshold precedence is host_override > field_record > default, and the resolved source is recorded on every decision
invariants.EB5: a threshold claimed by a request payload is ignored and the ignore is reported; entropy can refuse premature collapse and can never grant it
invariants.EB6: a non-finite or out-of-range threshold is a typed refusal, never a clamp that silently changes the gate
